verdict.rationale: OpenClaw's docs say memory is written as plain Markdown files in the agent's local workspace (default `~/.openclaw/workspace`), and the model only remembers what is saved to disk. Its Gateway runs on the user's own machine, so the store is local and in an open, human-readable format. The docs never describe tooling or workflows for inspecting, editing, or deleting memories, though plain files strongly imply it can be done. Missing for 10: documented inspect/edit/delete workflows for memory, guidance on how edits or deletions propagate to recall (e.g. indexes or active-memory history), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can inspect, edit, and delete what the assistant has remembered — the memory store lives on my machine in an open format
